saints.name: St. Helena
saints.title: Empress and Mother of Constantine
saints.shortBlurb: The mother of Constantine the Great, honored by tradition as the finder of the True Cross…
biography: Born about 248, most likely at Drepanum in Bithynia, a town later named Helenopolis for her, Helena was of humble station — Ambrose calls her a stable-maid. She bore the future emperor Constantine at Naissus about 272, and was put away when his father Constantius rose in the empire and took a wife of higher rank.

Her son's victory restored her: she returned to court, was named Augusta in 324, and embraced the Christian faith with an ardor her rank let her spend freely. About 326 she journeyed to the Holy Land, where she raised the Church of the Nativity at Bethlehem and that of the Ascension on the Mount of Olives.

Writers of the late fourth century, Rufinus and Ambrose among them, credit her with finding the True Cross near the Lord's tomb, three crosses lying hidden there. She died about 330 with her son at her side and was buried in her mausoleum on the Via Labicana. For her excavations at the holy places she is invoked by archaeologists, and for her late conversion, by converts.
saints.knownFor: Her pilgrimage and the tradition of finding the True Cross.
